items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: Mrs. Tuggle, who was the founder of the school, she was very close to my family then.

ctx.x: Well, I was, my father was a butcher. My mother, she was just a regular housewife. And then, I have also one sister and three other brothers. Well, I started right there at Tuogle Institute in Birmingham, Alabama. That school was right across the street from where I lived. See, all I had to do was just cross the

street and go, and jump the fence and there I was on the campus. Mrs. Tuggle, who was the founder of the school, she was very close to my family then. So, I used to play tin cans and things when the band come out at the end of the session to parade and close the school for that day. Well, I was too small to go out in the street. So, when I did, my father, I'm getting a little ahead of myself. My father passed (inaudible). He died when I was about 7 years old. Mrs. Tuggle told my family, said I'm gonna take that…

So, up to the age of 14 when she passed, and then I was able to play 'Taps.' And then they had me to play 'Taps' over her grave. All through that time, I played drums, alto horn, a little sax, a little baritone horn. The trumpet I picked up last.
